73572-the-shadow-girl.title: The Shadow Girl
73572-the-shadow-girl.creator: Unknown
73572-the-shadow-girl.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. We saw presently the wide area of a starlit night. A level landscape of vegetation. Grassy lawns; trees; a purpling brook, shimmering like a thread of pale silver in the starlight. The image was sharp now, distinct, and without suggestion of flicker. Every color rounded and full. Deep-toned nature, pale and serene in the starlight.

arxiv-1904-11985.title: Transmission of natural scene images through a multimode fibre
arxiv-1904-11985.creator: Piergiorgio Caramazza 1 , Oisín Moran 2 , Roderick Murray-Smith 2 , Daniele Faccio 1
arxiv-1904-11985.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Piergiorgio Caramazza 1 , Oisín Moran 2 , Roderick Murray-Smith 2 , Daniele Faccio 1. Abstract The optical transport of images through a multimode fibre remains an outstanding challenge with applications ranging from optical communications to neuro-imaging. State of the art approaches either involve measurement and control of the full complex field transmitted through the fibre or, more recently, training of artificial neural networks that however, are typically limited to image classes belong to the same class as the training data set.

arxiv-2012-01853.title: Structural Identifiability of a Pseudo-2D Li-ion Battery Electrochemical Model footnoteinfo Work supported by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council through grant EP/P005411/1- “Structured electrodes for improved energy storage.”
arxiv-2012-01853.creator: Ross Drummond, Stephen R. Duncan
arxiv-2012-01853.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Ross Drummond, Stephen R. Duncan. Growing demand for fast charging and optimised battery designs is fuelling significant interest in electrochemical models of Li-ion batteries. However, estimating parameter values for these models remains a major challenge. In this paper, a structural identifiability analysis was applied to a pseudo-2D Li-ion electrochemical battery model that can be considered as a linearised and decoupled form of the benchmark Doyle-Fuller-Newman model.

arxiv-2106-02577.title: Magnetic Structure of CoO
arxiv-2106-02577.creator: Ekkehard Krüger
arxiv-2106-02577.description: Abstract The paper reports theoretical evidence that the multi-spin-axis magnetic structure proposed in 1964 by van Laar actually does exist in CoO. This tetragonal spin arrangement produces both the strong tetragonal and the weaker monoclinic distortion experimentally observed in this material.

arxiv-2205-02906.title: Inflaton Dark Matter
arxiv-2205-02906.description: Abstract We discuss a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM) where a single real scalar field serves as both inflaton and dark matter. The corresponding Lagrangian contains the renormalizable interactions of the inflaton field. Quantum effects generally induce a non–minimal coupling to gravity which facilitates inflation consistent with the PLANCK constraints.

arxiv-2302-01080.title: Polyelectrolyte Knot Delocalization Induced by Counterion Condensation
arxiv-2302-01080.creator: Shensheng Chen, Tingtao Zhou
arxiv-2302-01080.description: Abstract Knots on ring polymers tend to be tight. For knots on charged polymers (polyelectrolytes), electrostatic repulsion among the monomers is considered to enhance the persistence length and further localize the knots. However, the effects of counterion condensation on knots behavior are not clear.

arxiv-2303-13819.title: Verification of ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} Adaptive Control using Verse Library: A Case Study of Quadrotors
arxiv-2303-13819.creator: Lin Song, Yangge Li, Sheng Cheng, Pan Zhao, Sayan Mitra, Naira Hovakimyan
arxiv-2303-13819.description: Abstract . ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} adaptive control ( ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} AC) is a control design technique that can handle a broad class of system uncertainties and provide transient performance guarantees. In this work-in-progress abstract, we discuss how existing formal verification tools can be applied to check the performance of ℒ 1 \mathcal{L}_{1} AC systems.

arxiv-2305-18258.title: Maximize to Explore: One Objective Function Fusing Estimation, Planning, and Exploration
arxiv-2305-18258.creator: Zhihan Liu, Miao Lu, Wei Xiong, Han Zhong, Hao Hu, Sirui Zheng, Zhuoran Yang, Zhaoran Wang
arxiv-2305-18258.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhihan Liu, Miao Lu, Wei Xiong, Han Zhong, Hao Hu, Sirui Zheng, Zhuoran Yang, Zhaoran Wang. In online reinforcement learning (online RL), balancing exploration and exploitation is crucial for finding an optimal policy in a sample-efficient way. To achieve this, existing sample-efficient online RL algorithms typically consist of three components: estimation, planning, and exploration. However, in order to cope with general function approximators, most of them involve impractical algorithmic components to incentivize exploration, such as optimization within data-dependent level-sets or complicated sampling procedures.

arxiv-2312-08923.title: Topology change and heterotic flux vacua
arxiv-2312-08923.creator: Yann Proto
arxiv-2312-08923.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yann Proto. We investigate the interrelation between topology and Narain T-duality of heterotic flux vacua. We present evidence that all 5 5 and 4 4 -dimensional Minkowski space heterotic flux backgrounds with 8 8 supercharges have a locus in the moduli space with a T-dual description in terms of a compactification on the product of a K3 surface with a circle or a torus. A test of this equivalence is provided by calculating the new supersymmetric index on both sides of the duality.

arxiv-2403-10448.title: Excluding cosmetic surgeries on hyperbolic 3-manifolds Thanks: August 8, 2026
arxiv-2403-10448.creator: David Futer, Jessica S. Purcell, Saul Schleimer
arxiv-2403-10448.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by David Futer, Jessica S. Purcell, Saul Schleimer. This paper employs knot invariants and results from hyperbolic geometry to develop a practical procedure for checking the cosmetic surgery conjecture on any given one-cusped manifold. This procedure has been used to establish the following computational results. First, we verify that all knots up to 19 crossings, and all one-cusped 3-manifolds in the SnapPy census, do not admit any purely cosmetic surgeries.

arxiv-2404-01203.title: Video Interpolation with Diffusion Models
arxiv-2404-01203.creator: Siddhant Jain, Daniel Watson, Eric Tabellion, Aleksander Hołyński, Ben Poole, Janne Kontkanen
arxiv-2404-01203.description: Abstract We present VIDIM, a generative model for video interpolation, which creates short videos given a start and end frame. In order to achieve high fidelity and generate motions unseen in the input data, VIDIM uses cascaded diffusion models to first generate the target video at low resolution, and then generate the high-resolution video conditioned on the low-resolution generated video.

arxiv-2404-09801.title: A Gray-Box Stability Analysis Mechanism for Power Electronic Converters
arxiv-2404-09801.creator: Rui Kong, Subham Sahoo, Yubo Song, and Frede Blaabjerg
arxiv-2404-09801.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rui Kong, Subham Sahoo, Yubo Song, and Frede Blaabjerg. This paper proposes a gray-box stability analysis mechanism based on data-driven dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) for commercial grid-tied power electronics converters with limited information on its control parameters and topology. By fusing the underlying physical constraints of the state equations into data snapshots, the system dynamic state matrix and input matrix are simultaneously approximated to identify the dominant system dynamic modes and eigenvalues using the DMD with control (DMDc) algorithm.

arxiv-2407-16455.title: Positive pressure matters in acoustic droplet vaporization
arxiv-2407-16455.creator: Samuele Fiorini, Anunay Prasanna, Gazendra Shakya, Marco Cattaneo, Outi Supponen
arxiv-2407-16455.description: Abstract Acoustically vaporizable droplets are phase-change agents that can improve the effectiveness of ultrasound-based therapies. In this study, we demonstrate that the compression part of an acoustic wave can generate tension that initiates the vaporization. This counter-intuitive process is explained by the occurrence of Gouy phase shift due to the focusing of the acoustic wave inside the droplet.

arxiv-2410-18457.title: Integrating Deep Feature Extraction and Hybrid ResNet-DenseNet Model for Multi-Class Abnormality Detection in Endoscopic Images
arxiv-2410-18457.description: Abstract This paper presents a deep learning framework for the multi-class classification of gastrointestinal abnormalities in Video Capsule Endoscopy (VCE) frames. The aim is to automate the identification of ten GI abnormality classes, including angioectasia, bleeding, and ulcers, thereby reducing the diagnostic burden on gastroenterologists.

arxiv-2412-09592.title: JWST PRIMER: strong evidence for the environmental quenching of low-mass galaxies out to z ≃ 𝟐 \mathbf{\textit{z}\simeq 2} Thanks: Scottish Universities Physics Alliance 2015 JWST PRIMER: strong evidence for the environmental quenching of low-mass galaxies out to z ≃ 𝟐 \mathbf{\textit{z}\simeq 2} –
arxiv-2412-09592.creator: M. L. Hamadouche, R. J. McLure, A. C. Carnall, D. J. McLeod, J. S. Dunlop, K. Whitaker, C. T. Donnan, R. Begley, T. M. Stanton, O. Almaini, J. Aird, F. Cullen, S. Cutler, A. M. Koekemoer
arxiv-2412-09592.description: Abstract We present the results of a study investigating the galaxy stellar-mass function (GSMF), size-mass relations and morphological properties of star-forming and quiescent galaxies over the redshift range 0.25 < z < 2.25 0.25<z<2.25 , using the JWST PRIMER survey.

arxiv-2501-10739.title: Computational Discovery of Chiasmus in Ancient Religious Text
arxiv-2501-10739.creator: Hope McGovern Hale Sirin Tom Lippincott
arxiv-2501-10739.description: Abstract Chiasmus, a debated literary device in Biblical texts, has captivated mystics while sparking ongoing scholarly discussion. In this paper, we introduce the first computational approach to systematically detect chiasmus within Biblical passages. Our method leverages neural embeddings to capture lexical and semantic patterns associated with chiasmus, applied at multiple levels of textual granularity (half-verses, verses).

pmc-10520025.title: Sexual segregation results in pronounced sex-specific density gradients in the mountain ungulate, Rupicapra rupicapra
pmc-10520025.creator: Hendrik Edelhoff, Cyril Milleret, Cornelia Ebert, Pierre Dupont, Thomas Kudernatsch, Alois Zollner, Richard Bischof, Wibke Peters
pmc-10520025.description: Sex-specific differences in habitat selection and space use are common in ungulates. Yet, it is largely unknown how this behavioral dimorphism, ultimately leading to sexual segregation, translates to population-level patterns and density gradients across landscapes. Alpine chamois (Rupicapra rupicapra r.) predominantly occupy habitat above tree line, yet especially males may also take advantage of forested habitats.

pmc-11369872.title: Meibomian gland dropout of upper eyelids as a novel biomarker for early diagnosis of primary Sjögren’s syndrome: a pilot study
pmc-11369872.creator: Jing Wu, Yongying Liang, Fanjun Shi, Xianghong Tu, Jingfa Zhang, Qinghua Qiu
pmc-11369872.description: Background:Early diagnosis of primary Sjögren’s syndrome (pSS) remains difficult due to its insidious onset.Objectives:To identify whether meibomian gland dropout (MGD) is a sensitive and noninvasive predictor of pSS by studying its association with histopathology in labial salivary gland biopsy in patients with clinically suspected pSS.Design:Prospective, randomized, multicenter, comparative effectiveness study.Methods:The study was conducted from July 2022 to July 2023.

pmc-11386031.title: Mechanical properties of intercellular tunneling nanotubes formed by different mechanisms
pmc-11386031.creator: Yanli Sun, Huikai Zhang, Ilya B Zavodnik, Hucheng Zhao, Xiqiao Feng
pmc-11386031.description: Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) that connect cells have been recognized as a pathway for long-range intercellular transport of diverse cargoes, including viruses, lysosomes or other organelles, Ca2+ and electrical signals. TNTs can initially be formed from thin finger-like actin assembly-driven protrusions or cell contacts and dislodgment.

pmc-11667648.title: PULPO: A framework for efficient integration of life cycle inventory models into life cycle product optimization
pmc-11667648.creator: Fabian Lechtenberg, Robert Istrate, Victor Tulus, Antonio Espuña, Moisès Graells, Gonzalo Guillén‐Gosálbez
pmc-11667648.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This work presents the PULPO (Python‐based user‐defined lifecycle product optimization) framework, developed to efficiently integrate life cycle inventory (LCI) models into life cycle product optimization. Life cycle optimization (LCO), which has found interest in both the process systems engineering and life cycle assessment (LCA) communities, leverages LCA data to go beyond simple assessments of a limited number of alternatives and identify the best possible product systems configuration subject to a manifold of choices, constraints, and objectives.

pmc-12428226.title: Identification of SUMO Proteins and Their Expression Profile During Induction of Somatic Embryogenesis in Medicago truncatula Gaertn.
pmc-12428226.creator: Anna Kujawska, Paulina Król, Karel Doležal
pmc-12428226.description: Somatic embryogenesis (SE) is a key plant regeneration technique involving the reprogramming of somatic cells into embryogenic structures. This developmental transition is regulated by complex genetic and epigenetic mechanisms, including post-translational modifications such as SUMOylation—the covalent attachment of small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteins to target proteins, influencing their function, stability, and interactions.

pmc-12690696.title: CNSM-02 Prognosis of Brain Metastases from Breast Cancer after Whole Brain Radiotherapy.
pmc-12690696.creator: Hicham Gazanayi, Othmane Saqri, Omar Baddi, Soukaina Morchid, Nabila Sellal, Mohammed El Hfid
pmc-12690696.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe incidence of brain metastases (BM) in patients with metastatic breast cancer ranges between 10-30%. Standard treatment includes surgery, whole brain radiotherapy (WBRT), and stereotactic radiotherapy. WBRT is frequently used due to limited stereotaxy access and multiple metastases prevalence.AimEvaluate the prognosis of patients treated with WBRT for breast cancer BM and identify predictive factors for overall survival and intracranial progression-free survival.MethodsThis retrospective study included 65 patients treated with WBRT for breast cancer BM between January 2020 and March 2023.

pmc-12930264.title: What Student Struggles do Instructors see? Teacher Knowledge of Students in Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences
pmc-12930264.creator: Alexandra C. Cooper, Marie D. Delcy, Erin L. Dolan
pmc-12930264.description: Course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) increase student access to research, providing opportunities for more students to engage with science practices and make novel science contributions. However, little is known about how to teach CUREs effectively. Effective CURE instruction relies on an instructor's knowledge of students, which is used to notice and respond to students as they conduct research.

pmc-13126020.title: Intelligent classification of dominant tree species in urban forests based on UAV hyperspectral remote sensing images
pmc-13126020.creator: Bin Lu, Shiping Ye, Zhican Bai, Chao Ye, Yanxin Xu, Kehang Zhou, Shukhrat Shokirov, Vladimir Golovko
pmc-13126020.description: SummaryUrban tree species classification is essential for green space management but is challenged by the fragmented spatial distributions of trees. To address this issue, this study employs a hyperspectral imagery-based classification method to improve the accuracy of urban forest identification.

pmc-13200850.title: TREATMENT OF INFERIOR POLE FRACTURE OF THE PATELLA IN ADULTS: SYNTHESIS OF CLINICAL EVIDENCE
pmc-13200850.creator: João Pedro de Melo, Stephanie Brandão, Diego David Vilte Martinez, Alessandra Masi, Carlos Gorios
pmc-13200850.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fractures of the Inferior pole patellar fracture (IPPF) affect the distal end of the bone, where the patellar tendon inserts, and are more common in young, active adults due to direct trauma or intense muscle contractions. This region, which is structurally more fragile and subjected to high tensile loads, becomes vulnerable to fractures that compromise the knee extensor mechanism, resulting in pain, functional limitation, and loss of mobility.
